data.title: Magic Boxes
data.statement:
Sam is shopping for some magic boxes. Each box has a value written on it.
The shop has all possible boxes with value ≥ {{2}} written on it. The shop is also quite magical, so it contains infinite boxes for each value.

Sam considers a group of boxes be <<Good>> when all of its values multiplied equals [[n]]. As a friend of Sam, please help him find out what is the maximum number of box(es) he can buy such that the group is <<Good>>, and the respective value of each box.

Example Explanation:
Given [[n]] = {{14}}. There are multiple ways to have a <<Good>> group of boxes, such as directly getting the box {{14}} itself. 

But the maximum number of boxes Sam can buy when the group of boxes is <<Good>> is {{2}}. So we print out {{2}} first.
The 2 boxes are {{2}} and {{7}}, since {{2 x 7 = 14}}. Thus we print out {{2 7}}.

Note that getting boxes {{1}} and {{14}} is invalid, since the shop doesn't have the box {{1}}.
Also getting boxes {{2}} and {{3}} is invalid, since {{2 x 3 ≠ 14}}.
data.outputDescription:
<<Line 1>>: The maximum number of box(es) Sam can buy when the group of boxes is <<Good>>.
<<Line 2>>: The respective value of each box in <<ascending order>>.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Sam is shopping for some magic boxes. Each box has a value written on it.
The shop has all possible boxes with value ≥ 2 written on it. The shop is also quite magical, so it contains infinite boxes for each value.

Sam considers a group of boxes be Good when all of its values multiplied equals n. As a friend of Sam, please help him find out what is the maximum number of box(es) he can buy such that the group is Good, and the respective value of each box.

Example Explanation:
Given n = 14. There are multiple ways to have a Good group of boxes, such as directly getting the box 14 itself.

But the maximum number of boxes Sam can buy when the group of boxes is Good is 2. So we print out 2 first.
The 2 boxes are 2 and 7, since 2 x 7 = 14. Thus we print out 2 7.

Note that getting boxes 1 and 14 is invalid, since the shop doesn't have the box 1.
Also getting boxes 2 and 3 is invalid, since 2 x 3 ≠ 14.
Input
Line 1: An integer n, denoting the *Good* value.
Output
Line 1: The maximum number of box(es) Sam can buy when the group of boxes is Good.
Line 2: The respective value of each box in ascending order.
Constraints
2 ≤ n ≤ 10^12
Example
Input
14
Output
2
2 7
